title: Fearless AI SDK Seam Deepening
problem: AI SDK contract hardening made behavior explicit, but several stream, diagnostics, tool, usage, and capability rules remain shallow caller knowledge.
objective: Deepen the remaining AI SDK contract seams into named modules with stronger locality, better leverage, executable projection rules, and less obsolete pass-through code.
gates: cargo nextest run -p siumai-spec -p siumai-core -p siumai-protocol-openai --no-fail-fast

evidence.summary: Post-hardening architecture review found six deepening candidates: OpenAI Responses stream state, diagnostics projection, tool ownership, capability gates, usage ledger, and core stream assembly.
ADR-0009 records crate-owned seam deepening as the architecture direction for the remaining AI SDK contract rules.
OpenAI Responses SSE converter state now has named owners for terminal buffering, replay hints, reasoning lifecycle, provider/custom tool ownership, and serializer allocation rules.
Public provider metadata and private diagnostics now have executable projection helpers used by stream response assembly and covered by spec/core/protocol regressions.
Provider-executed tool ownership now flows through a shared ToolExecutionOwner contract across spec prompt/UI/stream/tool views, core UI and stream projection, and OpenAI protocol adapters.

continue_policy.notes: Continue through AISD tasks in dependency order. Split provider-specific behavior only when a task proves the seam belongs outside the current crate. Hajimi adapter changes remain out of scope.
